results: 1. interictal EEG: runs of generalized polyspikes and spike-wave discharges at 2-3 Hz lasting 3-4 s, predominating bifrontally and occasionally shifting laterally

2. video-EEG monitoring of a typical event: ictal BODY TURNING, often preceded by head version, but the EEG shows classic GENERALIZED spike-wave or polyspike discharges WITHOUT consistent lateralization
3. antiseizure medication trial: responded to appropriate broad-spectrum antiseizure medication - NOT refractory
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy, a genetic generalized epilepsy syndrome
ALTERNATIVE 1: Frontal lobe epilepsy (less likely given the generalized ictal EEG without consistent lateralization)
ALTERNATIVE 2: Juvenile Absence Epilepsy (possible given the 2-3 Hz generalized spike-wave discharges)
ALTERNATIVE 3: Epilepsy with Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures Alone (if myoclonia is absent)
